description: Cologne Cathedral and Chartres Cathedral are documented major works of the European Gothic cathedral tradition.

description: Preston Central Bus Station and the Royal National Theatre are documented examples of British Brutalist architecture.

description: The Colosseum and Maison Carrée are surviving monuments of Roman imperial architecture: a Flavian amphitheatre and an Augustan imperial-cult temple.

source_refs.claim_note: Parco archeologico del Colosseo identifies the Colosseum as the 1st-century Flavian Amphitheatre commissioned by emperors and a symbol of the Roman Empire.
source_refs.title: The Colosseum

source_refs.claim_note: UNESCO identifies Maison Carrée as an Augustan Roman temple associated with imperial worship and the consolidation of the Roman Empire.
source_refs.title: The Maison Carrée of Nîmes

description: St. Peter's Basilica and Palladio’s Villa La Rotonda are documented works of Italian Renaissance architecture.

description: The dome of the Pantheon served as an explicit design reference for Bramante's plan and later dome studies for St. Peter's Basilica.

source_refs.claim_note: St. Peter's Basilica, Architecture / successive plans and dome sections: Bramante's dome was inspired by and closely followed the Pantheon, which remained an explicit reference for the dome design.
source_refs.title: St. Peter's Basilica — Wikipedia

description: St. Peter's Basilica and Brunelleschi’s Dome are major works of Italian Renaissance architecture and dome design.

source_refs.title: Brunelleschi's Dome

source_refs.claim_note: St. Peter’s Basilica reference identifies the church as Italian Renaissance architecture and documents its Renaissance dome design.

description: The Erechtheion and Parthenon belong to the Periclean building programme of the Athenian Acropolis and the classical Greek architectural tradition.

source_refs.claim_note: UNESCO Acropolis, Athens brief synthesis and criteria identify the Parthenon and Erechtheion among the principal monuments of the Periclean programme and classical Greek civilization.

description: The transformation of Paris's former Church of Sainte-Geneviève into a national mausoleum was modelled on the Pantheon in Rome.
